label: Rembrandt
clause: Shape a key so a triangle of brightness sits on the shadow cheek and the eye in that well still gleams.

label: Loop
clause: Place the key to throw a small hook of nose shade onto the opposite cheek, both eyes open.

label: Butterfly
clause: Place a key on the lens axis above the eyes so a butterfly-shaped shade sits under the nose and both cheeks stay open.

label: Paramount
clause: Drop a glamour key from slightly above the forehead with a scoop filling the eye sockets so cheekbones gleam and the upper lip wears a thin shade.

label: Split
clause: Put the key full side-on so one half of the face is lit and the other half falls to black, the nose as a border.

label: Broad
clause: Key the face-to-lens side so the larger visible cheek is bright and the distant cheek recedes into shade.

label: Short
clause: Key the averted side so the visible cheek is mostly shade and the smaller distant cheek is the bright one.

label: Clamshell
clause: Sandwich the face between an overhead key and a bounce from below so eye bags lift and catchlights sit in both upper and lower lids.

label: Beauty
clause: Flood the face with even frontal glamour so texture minimizes, catchlights sit at ten-and-two, and the background stays a clean pale cyc.

label: High-Key
clause: Lift almost all shadows so whites stay clean, the room feels bleached and airy, and contrast becomes a whisper.

label: Low-Key
clause: Let most of the room fall to black so a small island of brightness carves the face and the rest is withheld.

label: Silhouette
clause: Back the person against a brighter field so the body becomes a cutout and facial features vanish into the shape.

label: Semi-Silhouette
clause: Keep a hair of wrap on the cheek so the cutout body still has a hint of feature, not a pure black shape.

label: Chiaroscuro
clause: Pit a single pool against deep dark so form emerges from black as if carved, midtones scarce.

label: Rim
clause: Run a thin bright outline around the figure so they separate from a dark field without lighting the face.

label: Kicker
clause: Throw a raking accent from behind-the-side so the jaw and neck have a stripe of glare.

label: Hair Light
clause: Place a source above and behind so hair becomes a halo of strands and sparkle, the face still keyed separately.

label: Edge
clause: Skim an edge along a shoulder or prop so a specular line draws the silhouette without filling the front.

label: Wrap
clause: Let the key bend around the cheek so the terminator is gradual and pores stay readable into the shade.

label: Window
clause: Key from a visible window so the pane is the source, falloff marches across the room, and curtains shape the beam.

label: Practical Lamp
clause: Motivate the key from a visible lamp so the shade, bulb glow, and a pool on the table are the logic of the face.

label: Neon
clause: Key or accent from neon tubes so skin picks up saturated contour and the tubes themselves are graphic lines in the pane.

label: Fire
clause: Key from flame so the face flickers, orange on the closer plane, and shadows jump with the fire.

label: Screen
clause: Key from an unmarked display so the face is the color of the interface and the room around the glow dies.

label: Streetlamp
clause: Key from a streetlamp so a pool falls from above-the-street, moths in the beam, pavement bright.

label: Moonlight
clause: Top-fill with silver-cyan so crushed blacks hold, roof edges gleam, and skin is porcelain rather than honey.

label: Overcast Sky-Fill
clause: Wrap the person in shadowless sky from an overcast dome so there is no sun disk and no attached shade on the ground.

label: Hard Noon
clause: Put the sun overhead so noses and chins throw short attached shade, pavement bleaches, and eye sockets go dark.

label: Golden Hour
clause: Rake amber sidelight along brick and skin so long shadows stripe the street and highlights go honey.

label: Blue Hour
clause: Let residual sky cyan be the key while practicals just start to read, the world between sundown and full dark.

label: Tungsten-Daylight Mix
clause: Mix interior tungsten pools with blue window so skin is two temperatures at once, a lamp winning the cheek and sky winning the wall.

label: Hard Light
clause: Cast a small-source key so pores cast crisp self-shadows and the nose throws a sharp-edged triangle on the cheek.

label: Soft Light
clause: Wrap a large source so transitions on the jaw melt and speculars on skin become broad pillows.

label: Book Light
clause: Bounce a source into a diffusion frame so the face is wrapped by a second-generation glow with almost no specular bite.

label: Bounce
clause: Redirect the key off a wall or card so the source becomes a surface, not a lamp, and shade is open.

label: Diffusion
clause: Put diffusion in the beam so the source size grows, lashes cast gentler shade, and hot spots bloom.

label: Grid
clause: Fit a grid so spill dies and the beam becomes a controlled oval on the face, walls staying dark.

label: Snoot
clause: Snoot the source into a small circle so only an eye or a product highlight exists, the rest falling off.

label: Shaft
clause: Cut a shaft through haze so a visible beam is architecture and motes travel inside it.

label: Volumetric
clause: Thicken the air with haze so every beam becomes a volume and the room is carved in light-solid.

label: Blinds Breakup
clause: Let blinds throw bars across face and wall so the person is printed with the window's geometry.

label: Leaf Dapple
clause: Let canopy holes dapple the person with moving coin-spots of sun and leaf-shaped shade.

label: Water Caustics
clause: Throw water caustics so wriggling bright veins crawl over face, tile, or hull.

label: Warm Key Cool Fill
clause: Key from an amber practical and fill the wells with window cyan so skin is honey on the key side and steel in the shade.

label: Motivated Mix
clause: Let every source on the face be justified by a visible lamp, window, or fire so nothing feels added.

label: Cameo
clause: Light only the person against a dead-black field so they are a cameo and the room does not exist.

label: White Limbo
clause: Surround with a seamless bright cyc so the person floats in tone, almost no horizon.

label: Noir Slash
clause: Slash a barn-door bar across the eyes so the rest of the face is withheld in crime-story dark.

label: Cross Key
clause: Key two people from opposite sides so each is bright on the outer cheek and they share a dark middle.

label: Top Light
clause: Drop the key from directly above so eye sockets hollow, the nose becomes a sundial, and hair becomes a lid of brightness.

label: Underlight
clause: Key from below so the brow ridges invert, the face becomes a mask, and ceilings catch the bounce.

label: Three-Point
clause: Combine a key, a weaker fill, and a back edge so form, shade, and separation all read at once.

label: One-Point
clause: Use a single source only so falloff is honest and the distant wall dies.

label: Back Halo
clause: Let a rear source bloom the hair into a luminous wreath while a whisper of front fill keeps the eyes.

label: Candle
clause: Key from a candle so the face becomes a small living island, flicker in the eyes, hands close to the flame.

label: Flashlight
clause: Key from a handheld torch so a bouncing disk of brightness hunts the room and the beam becomes a character.

label: Headlights
clause: Key from vehicle headlights so the person is blasted from road level, long shadows thrown up a wall.

label: Signage Glow
clause: Let unmarked signage wash the face in saturated color so letters or shapes of the sign spill onto skin.

label: Fridge Glow
clause: Open a fridge so the person is keyed by the cold interior, food silhouettes in the closer plane.

label: North Window
clause: Key from a north-facing window so the wrap is even and painterly, open shade without a sun patch.

label: Skylight Well
clause: Key from a skylight well so a column of brightness hits the floor and faces enter or leave that column.

label: Ceiling Bounce
clause: Bounce the key off the ceiling so the room becomes a gentle downlight, eye sockets filled, lamps not visible as sources.

label: Wall Bounce
clause: Bounce off a side wall so the key arrives as a big vertical surface and one side of the nose is open.

label: Paper Lantern
clause: Key from a paper lantern so the source becomes a glowing orb in the pane and the wrap is omnidirectional and kind.

label: Bare Bulb
clause: Hang a bare bulb so it becomes a star in the pane, sharp shade, and the socket is part of the furniture.

label: Fresnel Spot
clause: Spot with a fresnel so the beam has a crisp circle, barn-doorable edges, and theatrical falloff on the floor.

label: Projector Beam
clause: Key from a projector so the face wears the image's color and dust lives in the throw.

label: Lightning
clause: Light with a lightning flash so the scene becomes a single white instant, rain frozen, then implied dark.

label: Campfire
clause: Circle a campfire so faces are orange islands in woods-dark, sparks rising through the pane.

label: Stove
clause: Key from a stove or burner so the cook's face is underlit by flame and pots throw copper bounce.

label: Vanity
clause: Key from a bathroom vanity ring or strip so the mirror person is evenly frontal and tiles bounce white.

label: Interrogation
clause: Drop a single overhead practical so the table becomes a bright desk, faces sweat in a cone, corners of the room vanish.

label: Storefront Spill
clause: Let a storefront spill onto the sidewalk so the person is half in shop-color and half in street dark.

label: Sunset Blinds
clause: Let late sun through blinds so amber bars crawl the wall and the face is sliced by the same geometry.

label: Open Shade
clause: Stand the person in open shade so sky is the key, no sun patch, and color shifts slightly steel without going moonlit.

label: Desert Sun
clause: Blast from a desert sun so bounce off sand fills from below, contrast is brutal, and squint is part of the face.

label: Forest Gloom
clause: Key a dim forest so trunks are dark columns, a clearing is the source, and moss eats bounce.

label: Underwater Blue
clause: Key underwater so caustics plus blue fill, the surface a bright lid, skin going cyan.

label: Night Window Exterior
clause: Shoot a person inside from outside after dark so the window becomes a diorama of tungsten and the street around it is black.

label: Fluorescent Office
clause: Key from overhead office tubes so skin shifts slightly green-grey, ceiling tiles grid the bounce, and shadows are double.

label: Sodium Street
clause: Bathe in sodium-vapor amber so the street is monochrome honey and other colors collapse.

label: Rain-Wet Bounce
clause: Let wet pavement bounce sources back so faces get a second key from below and highlights streak.

label: Fog Street
clause: Mute sources with fog so each lamp becomes a glowing blob and the person appears as they enter a pool.

label: Smoke Volume
clause: Add smoke in layers so a doorway beam becomes a wall of brightness the person has to walk through.

label: Stained Glass
clause: Key through stained glass so colored geometry paints the floor and the face wears patches of ruby and cobalt.

label: Aquarium
clause: Key from a tank so fish-shadows and a blue-green wash crawl the nearby cheek, the glass a practical.

label: Vending Glow
clause: Key from a vending machine so the face is the color of the cabinet and rows of unmarked goods are the set.

label: Phone Screen Key
clause: Key from a phone screen so only the eyes and hands exist in a small rectangle of interface glow.

label: Laptop Key
clause: Key from a laptop so the face is the page color, keyboard dim, and the room around the lid is gone.

label: TV Flicker
clause: Key from a television so the face pulses with scene changes and the sofa is an island in the dark.

label: Match Strike
clause: Light with a struck match so for a beat the face becomes a cave painting, then the flame settles in the fingers.

label: Oven
clause: Key from an open oven so the cook is underlit by the cavity, racks as bars, heat implied in the glow.

label: Silk Overhead
clause: Stretch a silk overhead so noon is tamed into a large even source, eyes open, ground shade still present but gentle.

label: Negative Fill
clause: Flag the fill side with black so the key stays, but the shadow cheek goes to velvet and cheekbone pops.

label: Rim Only
clause: Kill the key and keep only a rim so the person is an outline drawing against dark.

label: Beauty and Hair
clause: Combine even frontal beauty with a hair halo so fashion gloss and strand separation both read.

label: Split plus Kicker
clause: Split the face and add a kicker on the dark side so the withheld cheek has a thin lifeline of edge.

label: Cool Key Warm Fill
clause: Key from a north sky and bounce a tungsten lamp into the shadow cheek so the lit plane is porcelain and the dark plane is candle.

label: Golden Rim Cool Shadow
clause: Rim with late-sun gold and let the front fill be blue shade so the outline is honey and the face is steel.

label: Blue Hour City Mix
clause: Mix residual-sky cyan with shop practicals so the person is cyan on top and amber in the storefront spill.

label: Practicals vs Blue Window
clause: Let table lamps win the faces while a blue window claims the back wall, two worlds in one room.

label: Noon Bounce Fill
clause: Keep overhead noon but bounce a card into the eye sockets so the brutal sun stays and the face remains readable.

label: Overcast plus Practicals
clause: Keep overcast sky-fill and add interior lamps so the room is even from the windows and honey from the fixtures.

label: Operating Room
clause: Flood from multiple overhead surgical sources so there are no hiding places, skin is clinical, steel specular.

label: Mirror-Ball Breakup
clause: Break the room with a mirror-ball so coins of light crawl walls and the dancer is spotted by moving dots.

label: Snow Bounce
clause: Let snow on the ground bounce sky back into faces so the undersides of brows are filled and the world is bright from below.

label: Doorway Sun
clause: Let sun through a doorway so a rectangle of brightness becomes a solid on the floor and a person stepping through is ignited.

label: Skimming Side
clause: Skim the key along the wall so texture of brick or plaster rakes and the person is half in that rake.

label: Beauty Fill Below
clause: Add a bounce just for beauty so eyelashes throw tiny shade upward and the under-eye is cleaned.

label: Hair and Edge
clause: Combine a hair halo with a shoulder edge so the whole outline is separated without lighting the shirt front.

label: Table-Lamp Key
clause: Plant the key in a table lamp next to the person so the shade pattern prints on the wall and the closer cheek is the hot side.

label: Fireplace Key
clause: Key from a fireplace so the hearth is the source, faces orange toward it, backs going to room-dark.

label: Store Interior
clause: Key from store-aisle overheads so rows of goods are the practicals and the person is shopper-lit, fluorescent and even.

label: Moon Through Trees
clause: Let moonlight through trees so silver dapple moves on the face and the woods stay a black lace.

label: Overcast Beach
clause: Fill from overcast beach so sand becomes a giant bounce, sky is the key, and there is almost no eye-socket dark.

label: Industrial Mix
clause: Mix greenish industrial tubes with a tungsten work lamp so the shed is two chemical colors.

label: Bathroom Mirror
clause: Key from a mirrored bathroom so the person is doubled, tiles specular, and the source is the vanity in the glass.

label: Car Interior Night
clause: Key a car interior after dark from dash glow and passing street pools so faces pulse as lamps go by.

label: Tent Diffusion
clause: Surround with a diffusion tent so product or face is wrapped one-hundred-eighty degrees, speculars huge and polite.

label: Flagged Face
clause: Flag the key so a barn-door or flag cuts the chest and only the face wears the beam.

label: Checkerboard Shadow
clause: Throw a lattice or grate shadow so the body becomes a checkerboard of brightness and withheld squares.

label: Lace Curtain
clause: Let lace curtains print floral shade on the face so the window's fabric becomes a tattoo of light.

label: Water Bounce Up
clause: Bounce a source off water so the ceiling and jaw get moving bright veins from below.

label: Amber Practical Pool
clause: Sit the person in a pool from an amber practical so they can step in or out of being lit, the rest of the room dead.

label: Cyan Moon Edge
clause: Put a cyan moon-edge on the profile so the outline is ice and the front of the face is almost unlit.

label: Dual-Color Split
clause: Split the face not only in brightness but in color, one cheek amber, the other cyan, the nose the border.

label: White Cyc High-Key
clause: Flood a white cyc so the person is almost shadowless, fashion-catalog bright, seams of clothes still readable.

label: Black Limbo
clause: Drop the surround to black so the person becomes a sculpted island, no set, only form.

label: Rain Window Key
clause: Key from a rain-streaked window so the face wears moving rivulets of brightness and the pane is the source.

label: Welding Flash
clause: Light with a welding flash so for a frame the shed is white, then the afterimage lives in the dark.

label: Headlamp
clause: Key from a forehead lamp so the beam looks where the person looks, a disk of brightness on the task.

label: Porch Light
clause: Key from a porch fixture so insects crowd the source, the face entering a yellow-white pool at the door.

label: Multi-Candle
clause: Key from many candles so the table becomes a constellation of small sources, faces stitched from several directions.

label: Venetian Bars
clause: Throw venetian slat-bars across a torso so the body becomes a musical staff of brightness, not a full window print on the wall.

label: Bounce-Card Fill
clause: Hold a white card just out of pane so the shadow cheek opens a stop without adding a second lamp in the set.

label: Black Wrap
clause: Wrap black around the key so spill dies on the walls and the face becomes a controlled island in a dark room.
